$comment: GENERATED BY build.mjs — edit src/vercel.template.json, not vercel.json.
The script-src hash is computed from the assembled inline <script>, so it
changes whenever the app changes. `node build.mjs --check` fails if the
committed vercel.json no longer matches the committed index.html, which is
the failure that would otherwise take the whole site down in production
while every local check still passed. index.html is the one page with the
script inline; every other page loads the same bytes from
assets/app.<hash>.js, which 'self' allows. index.html is no longer
deployed (.vercelignore; plan item 1.2), and its hash stays: were a host
to deploy it anyway, / would be index.html, and its script must still run.
The second hash names the
small script every page carries in its head (build.mjs, FIRST_SCRIPT),
which runs before the first paint: the theme kept, and whether the page
served is this reader's.
$comment-rewrites: One rewrite per route in ROUTES (src/js/35-ui.js), written by build.mjs in
place of the marker below. A route without a parameter goes to its own page
(pages/<route>.html, the site root to pages/home.app.html: index.html,
linked like every other page, plan item 1.2), whose <head> is the one
the router sets there; a parameter route (/company/:id …) to the generic page,
pages/generic.app.html: the site root's head and the app, with no page in it
Every exact path is listed before any :param, and each is explicit: nothing
relies on Vercel checking its files before its rewrites. The site root is
the one address a file would answer first (index.html), and .vercelignore
keeps that file off the host, so the rewrite of / is reached.
There is no catch-all. It answered 200 with the homepage for any address,
so a dead link was a soft 404. Anything no rewrite and no file answers is
served 404.html with status 404: the shell with the not-found head and
noindex, on which the app draws its not-found card. /data/ and /_vercel/
are never rewritten: they are files, or they are absent.
serve.mjs reads these rewrites, trailingSlash and 404.html from vercel.json,
so every local harness is served what Vercel serves.
$comment-trailingSlash: /pricing/ opens the pricing page in the router, which drops a trailing
slash. The catch-all served it; a rewrite's source matches its path
exactly. false makes Vercel answer 308 to the same address without the
slash, keeping the query, so each page has one address.
$comment-redirects: An address ending in /index.html means the folder it names: /pricing/index.html
is /pricing. Answered as an unknown address it got the 404 page, where the
router took /pricing for a folder the app is deployed in (BASE, 35-ui.js),
drew the homepage instead of the not-found card and asked for
/pricing/data/us.json. A 308 to the folder's own address answers it: a route
there opens, anything else is the not-found page.
The site root's own /index.html (not matched by :path+, which needs a
segment) was served as the file: the app inline, 3.5MB. / is
pages/home.app.html since plan item 1.2, and index.html is not deployed
(.vercelignore); /index.html is a 308 to /, the query kept. Redirects are
applied before the file system, so this holds even on a host that deployed
the file.
A FILED COMPANY BY ITS ID (the 9 Oct 2026 audit, item #7: deep links).
/company/AAPL-SEC, the address a company's id gives (BY_ID, 25-universe.js),
was served the generic page: no h1, no summary, the company drawn only once
the script had loaded the filings. Each SEC filer's id, in any case, is a
308 to the company's own pre-rendered page (/company/aapl-apple-inc), the
query (?tab=…) kept. One rule per filer, written by build.mjs in place of
the marker below from data/us.json (companyIdRedirects): a character class
per letter, because a source is case-sensitive. An illustrative company's
address, and an id no company has, are left to the router as before.

$comment: Versioned data. dataUrl() appends ?v=<content hash> from DATA_VERSIONS,
which build.mjs stamps into the app, so a URL's contents can never
change — a year of immutable caching is safe and a changed file simply
arrives under a new URL. us.json alone is 1.4MB; before this it was
re-fetched on every navigation because fetchJson sent no-store.
An UNVERSIONED /data request (a licensed-lane file that only exists on
the reader's own machine) still gets no-store from fetchJson itself.
max-age here is the CDN's and the browser's ceiling, not a floor.
The renders build.mjs puts into each page (prerender/, prerender.mjs) are
files of the repository, so the host serves them too, each at its own
address: a page's content as a document of its own, with no head, no
canonical and no disclosure, beside the page that carries it. Not for an
index (robots.txt disallows them as well). Its own header, so this rule
and the pages' rule below never set the same one.
My Dashboard (/app) and the Scanner (/app/scanner and every address
under it: its dashboard, the setup builder, setups, alerts) are a
reader's own lane: kept out of search, and readable by any fetcher
(plan item 1.1, the owner's decision D2 of 5 Oct 2026). robots.txt
disallowed them, so a fetcher that follows it could not read
/app/scanner or /app/scanner/setups/new at all, although each serves a
fresh visitor's page; and a crawler that may not fetch a page never
reads a noindex on it. So robots.txt allows them, and this header says
noindex on every response at those addresses. Not /app/equities or any
other address under /app: those are product pages, as before. Its own
header, which no other rule sets on these addresses.
The app's script, written once by build.mjs for every page but
index.html (which carries it inline): assets/app.<first 12 hex of its
SHA-256>.js, index.html's inline script byte for byte. Its name changes
whenever a byte of it does, so a browser may keep it for a year without
asking again (immutable), and a page names the one it was built with.
The source is the current file's exact address, filled in by the build:
a name no longer written is a 404, and not cached for a year. The
content type is said, not left to the host's guess, so serve.mjs and
Vercel send the same one; nosniff holds the browser to it. It is
allowed by script-src 'self' in the pages' policy below.
The app's stylesheet, the same way: index.html's inline <style>, byte
for byte, at assets/app.<hash>.css. Allowed by style-src 'self'.
The app shell carries its own version, so it must always be revalidated.
no-store rather than must-revalidate: a stale shell paired with a new
data manifest is the one combination that renders wrong numbers, and
the file is a single 1.3MB gzip-compressible response on a CDN edge.
Every address but data/ and the two app files above, which the build
names in the lookahead: each header of each response comes from one
rule, whatever order the host applies overlapping rules in.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' '@CSP_HASH' '@CSP_FIRST_HASH'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'
geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()
